Vainly
VAYN-lee
adv. (emptily; to no purpose; without ground)
Latin vanus, empty, through French vain, with the ending -ly. In Colossians 2:18 it renders the Greek eike, without cause or ground.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Paul warns the Colossians against a devout-looking error: “Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind” (Colossians 2:18). Every term is chosen. The humility is voluntary — self-chosen, not commanded; the worship is directed to angels; the teacher intrudes into what he has not seen; and the result is a man swollen with nothing. Vainly puffed up is the apostle's judgment on asceticism and mystical speculation together: the inflation is real and the content is empty. The Authorized Version uses vainly once. The next verse gives the fatal defect: “And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God” (Colossians 2:19). That is the test the dictionary applies to every spirituality offered to Christians — angelic hierarchies, visionary experience, self-imposed severity, or the modern varieties. Does it hold the Head? If it does not, the growth is swelling, not increase.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): VAINLY, adverb In vain; to no purpose; ineffectually; idly; foolishly.

2. Idly; foolishly.

VAIN, adjective Empty; worthless; having no substance, value or importance.

Key Scripture

Col 2:18 — "Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,"

Col 2:19 — "And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God."

Col 2:23 — "Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body; not to any honour of the satisfying of the flesh."

Modern Corruption

Self-chosen severity and visionary experience are still marketed as depth; Paul calls them empty inflation that does not hold the Head.

expand to see more

Colossians 2:18 describes a permanent species of error, and its modern forms are easy to name: contemplative techniques imported from outside Scripture, angel-devotion, claimed visions and private revelations, graded severities of diet and discipline presented as spiritual advancement. Verse 23 grants that such things have indeed a shew of wisdom. A shew is all they have.

The principle to recover is verse 19. Growth in the Christian life comes through the Head, by joints and bands, in the body — that is, through Christ by ordinary means in the church. Anything that advertises increase while loosening the grip on Christ is producing swelling, and Paul's word for it is vainly puffed up.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Latin vanus, empty; renders Greek eike, without ground, in Paul's verdict on will-worship at Colossians 2:18.

expand to see more

Latin vanus, empty or void; French vain.

Greek eike, without cause, groundlessly, to no purpose.

Colossians 2:18 is the only place the Authorized Version uses vainly.

Voluntary humility renders a phrase for self-chosen, uncommanded severity.

Colossians 2:19 gives the test: holding, or not holding, the Head.

Usage

"a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels"

"vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind"

"not holding the Head"
